title: Maintaining the Status Quo: Capturing Invariant Relations for OOD Spatiotemporal Learning

problem.claim: Spatiotemporal models can suffer distribution shifts between training and testing data, creating an out-of-distribution learning problem, while segment-level heterogeneity and complex spatial dependencies make invariant relation extraction difficult.

gap.claim: Few studies address out-of-distribution problems in temporal regression, and fewer still focus on spatiotemporal learning.

contributions.claim: The paper introduces CauSTG, a causal spatiotemporal learning framework intended to transfer invariant relations to out-of-distribution scenarios.
CauSTG treats temporal steps as environments, transforms spatiotemporal relations into learnable parameters, and partitions temporal steps into sub-environments based on distinctive trend patterns.

CauSTG uses a spatiotemporal consistency learner and a hierarchical invariance explorer to filter stable relations through bidirectional spatial consistency, disentangled seasonal-trend patterns, and local and global variation-based invariances.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments reportedly show that CauSTG improves performance by at most 10.26% over the best baselines.
The authors report that visualized invariant relations can interpret physical rationales.
The appendix and code are reported to be available in a GitHub repository.

narrative_sequence.summary: Spatiotemporal learning is important for urban digitalization.
Distribution shifts, limited prior work on out-of-distribution temporal regression, and heterogeneous spatial-temporal structure create the target challenge.
The authors propose CauSTG to transfer invariant spatiotemporal relations to out-of-distribution scenarios.
The framework defines temporal environments, reorganizes samples by trend-pattern sub-environments, and learns stable relations through consistency and hierarchical invariance modules.
The authors report performance gains over baselines and interpretable visualized invariant relations.

source_observation.claim: The framework treats temporal steps as environments and separates them into sub-environments according to distinctive trend patterns.

interpretation.claim: When temporal data contains heterogeneous periodic behavior, organizing samples by environment-like temporal regimes may help isolate relations that remain stable across distribution shifts.

application.claim: For spatiotemporal regression under changing conditions, test regime-aware temporal partitioning before learning invariant relations.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether the approach generalizes beyond the described spatiotemporal settings or how it performs when trend patterns are not distinctive.

source_observation.claim: The method jointly uses consistency learning and hierarchical filtering to extract local and global stable relations.

interpretation.claim: Combining local and global invariance signals may reduce reliance on relations that are predictive only in a narrow context.

application.claim: In other distribution-shifted relational data, consider jointly evaluating consistency at multiple structural scales.

exception.claim: The abstract does not report ablations showing the separate contribution of the consistency learner and hierarchical invariance explorer.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the datasets, baselines, evaluation metrics, or experimental settings.
The abstract does not provide the exact meaning of the reported 10.26% improvement.
The abstract does not describe the out-of-distribution scenarios or the causal assumptions used by CauSTG.
The abstract does not report ablation results, statistical uncertainty, or computational costs.
